Prepare application documents and check the result

Use this workflow when a recipient asks for an ordered PDF and a separate photo or signature. First read their current instructions: some require separate files instead of a combined document. The examples below are synthetic, not official application requirements.

Requirements · PDF example · Signature example · Final checks

1. Record the receiving portal’s requirements

  • Which documents are required, and in what order?
  • One PDF or separate files? What is the maximum size per file?
  • For images: accepted format, width, height, minimum and maximum KB, and the KB convention.
  • Any rules for legibility, background, date, signatures or certification?

Do not alter a digitally signed or certified document unless the recipient permits it. These PDF tools create edited copies and may lose forms, bookmarks or valid signatures.

2. Practice a three-page submission

Download the one-page cover and two-page attachments. They contain no personal information.

  1. Open Merge PDF and select both samples.
  2. Use the file arrows to put the cover first, then merge and download.
  3. Open the downloaded file in a PDF reader. It should have three pages: the cover followed by attachments 2 and 3.
  4. If your recipient only requested the cover and last attachment, open Extract Pages, select the merged file and enter 1,3. The result should have two pages.
Known outputs from these exact samples
OperationExpected outputReference file
Merge cover, then attachments3 pages; 1,608 bytes in this buildThree-page reference
Extract 1,3 from the merged PDF2 pages; cover then final attachmentTwo-page reference

Compare page content and order, not file hashes. Metadata can change the byte count. These references are generated using yourPDF’s processing code; they are not evidence that arbitrary documents will preserve every feature.

If the PDF exceeds the recipient’s limit

Check whether you included unnecessary documents, but remove pages only when permitted. Optimize PDF can reduce structural overhead; it does not downsample scan images. For an image-heavy PDF, re-export from the original scanner or document application at an allowed resolution, then check legibility. Read why a PDF may not shrink.

3. Prepare a separate signature image

Try the 1,000 × 400 practice drawing in Signature resizer. This is a drawing, not a real signature.

  1. Turn off the dimension-ratio link. Enter 300 pixels wide and 100 pixels high.
  2. Choose Fit and PNG. Set minimum size to 0 KB and maximum to 100 KB; select 1 KB = 1,000 bytes. These are practice settings only.
  3. Prepare the image. Fit should place a 250 × 100 drawing inside a 300 × 100 canvas, with 25 white pixels on each side.
  4. Download it and select that saved file in Requirement checker. Enter the same requirements and inspect the drawing visually.

Crop fills the canvas by removing content at the top and bottom for this sample. For your own signature, inspect every pen stroke. If the portal requires JPG, select JPG and check the resulting bytes again; changing the extension alone does not convert the image. See the pixels and KB guide.

4. Check the actual saved files before submitting

  • Open each saved file independently, not only its in-tool preview.
  • Check first and last pages, total page count, order, orientation and readable details.
  • Compare the file’s byte size with the portal’s convention. 100 decimal KB is 100,000 bytes; 100 binary KB is 102,400 bytes.
  • Keep photos and signatures separate when requested. Do not merge them into the PDF by assumption.
  • Use a clear filename and retain the original files until acceptance.

A technical pass is not a guarantee of acceptance. yourPDF cannot assess identity, authenticity, required content or every portal rule. If a practice task fails, report the tool, settings and browser; do not send private documents.
